utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's cross-examination, Mr. Zecevic or Mr. Pantelic. Who will begin? Mr. Pantelic will begin, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Bicic, I'm Pantelic, attorney from Belgrade, representing Mr. Blagoje Simic. Mr. Bicic, among others, you gave two statements to the Prosecutor. One was given in the period between the 22nd and the 24th of February, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And your second statement was given on the 12th of March, 1998; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the part of your statement relating to a description of the members of the paramilitary units, a certain Lugar, Beli, Zec? Do you remember giving a description of their appearance?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember making a description of their appearance. Whether those were paramilitary units, as far as I was able to see, they were units that were part of all the units that were in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would like the assistance of Mr. Usher because I have a statement here of this witness, and he's going to read relevant portions which are connected to this particular question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Now, which one? Which one of the statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the statement in B/C/S version. He gave it between 22nd and 24 February, 1995, to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's strictly related to the descriptions of these persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could counsel identify the page number for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is the B/C/S version 00637684.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just the page number on the bottom because we can follow along in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There is no page on the bottom of B/C/S version. There is only your ERN number. Roughly saying, Mr. Weiner, it's maybe the second page of your English version, where he is speaking about the -- immediately after the arrest of 18 April, he is speaking about these particular persons. Because my English version is totally illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, you're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Mr. Bicic, somewhere around the middle of the page, you will see a description of Lugar, this man called Lugar. Could you read that out for us, please? Have you found the passage?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Will you read it out aloud, please, what Lugar looked like.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I have to read it out aloud?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, so that the interpreters can follow.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Lugar was born maybe in 1953 or 1954. He was about 180 centimetres in height; 90 to 100 kilogrammes in weight; strong build; oval face; prominent cheekbones and jaw; brown, short hair; brown eyebrows --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Could you read slowly, because the interpreter has to interpret.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Lugar was born in 1953 or 1956. He was about 180 centimetres in height. He weighed between 90 to 100 kilogrammes. He had a strong build; oval face; prominent cheekbones and jaw; short, brown hair; brown eyebrows; had a boxer kind of nose, scars or cuts on his face due to boxing or whatever."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you just read that last sentence as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this one, that I had seen him before on TV in boxing bouts?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's right. Thank you. Tell me, please, Mr. Bicic: How do you know that Lugar was born sometime between 1953 and 1956? Did you know that in those days in Samac in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I assume that, and that is why I said between 1953 and 1956.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but these descriptions are correct, are they not: his height, his weight? You still abide by what you said then?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Roughly, that's what he looked like at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. Will you please read out two paragraphs further down the page, where it says, "Beli was born," the paragraph relating to Beli.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Beli --"

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Slowly, please, because of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Beli was born roughly in 1958 or 1960. He was about 170 centimetres in height, also of strong build. He had very light hair, which is why they called him "Beli," which means "white." He had a pudgy nose.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So regarding Beli, you also roughly thought that was his age. You didn't hear that from someone else; this is what you assumed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is my assumption that I referred to when describing the man.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But regarding his description, his height and appearance in those days, that is a correct description, is it not? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, roughly so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please be kind enough and read out the sentence starting with the word "Zec," a nickname of another member of those units.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Zec was 28 to 30 years old. He was about 200 centimetres in height. He had short, black hair. He had a strong characteristic Montenegrin accent. I later learnt he was from Pljevlja, in Montenegro. Once Zec kicked me in the chest, saying that he was a Muslim too, as his mother was a Muslim, but he was on the right side, and why wasn't I on the right side? That is how I remember him."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So in this particular case too, with respect to this person named Zec, you spoke to that person, and therefore you can be certain of this description, that he was about 200 centimetres tall and had short, black hair?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't talk to that person, but that person spoke to me while beating me. Therefore, I said "roughly," or "approximately." I was describing the man that I saw several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that the description is quite accurate regarding his height and his hair; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Bicic, when did you see Lugar on television in boxing bouts?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you said that in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that, but I can't remember. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please turn to the next page, and you will see a paragraph beginning with the words "Stevo Todorovic." Will you read that out, please.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Stevo Todorovic was born approximately in 1955. About 185 to 190 centimetres in height; fat; ugly face; light brown hair. He wore a green camouflage uniform with a 4-S insignia and a green beret with a Kokarda on it. Even before the war, people avoided him."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Had you seen Stevan Todorovic before the war?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was a regular customer, on a daily basis, in our pizza parlour. He would come several times a day, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please read out now the third paragraph from this one, when you talk about an officer called Srdjan?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Will you read that part out, please?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Later" --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, below that, the paragraph below that.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Srdjan was about 25 years old, he was about 165 centimetres in height. He had brown hair, wore a JNA officer uniform, and on his shirt was a metal bar with two yellowish stripes showing that he was a lieutenant."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So, Mr. Bicic, on the basis of all these details from your statement, we can agree, can't we, that you give quite a precise description of people regarding their physical appearance, their height, the colour of their hair, and the other personal details; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly the way I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you are able to give quite a specific description. You worked in a restaurant, you met a lot of people, you're able to describe people, and I think you do that very well, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but will you please mitigate that a little?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Bicic, are you aware of the nickname Debeli?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the person with that nickname?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, will you please turn to the page marked 689, the last three numbers being 689? Will you please read out slowly, because of the interpreters, the last paragraph on that page, beginning with the words "on the 13th of May"? Please read that out for us.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the 13th of May, they took us back to Bosanski Samac to be released, but they took us to the secondary school. There were about 47 of us who were transferred to the secondary school in Samac. The guy we called Minus was in charge of our transfer. His group took us as far as Obudovac where we were taken over by another group of policemen in Bosanski Samac. They wore the police uniforms of the former Yugoslavia, but their insignia were Serb. As we were getting off the bus, they beat us, the local Chetniks beat us, who were wearing police uniforms. They were from the environs of the town. Stevo Todorovic was the chief of police in charge of the secondary school. When we arrived in Samac, we stopped in front of the police station, and while we were inside the bus, I heard Todorovic giving orders for us to be taken to a sports hall of the secondary school. There, we were received by policemen. One of them was drunk, and his rifle was unlocked, which he used to beat my brother so that the rifle went off, hitting the bus."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Will you be kind enough and turn the page and read the next paragraph relating to this incident?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "When we were placed in the sports hall, we were lined up against a wall and a policeman shot above our heads with a pistol, a Scorpion. The shooting above our heads happened inside the sports hall. That night, another group of people was brought in. A couple of men were beaten up, one of them was Kemal Atic. So several people, one of whom was Kemal Atic, were beaten up. The next day, Stevo Todorovic came with a fat man whose name was Srecko Radovanovic, Debeli, escorted by about ten soldiers. They inspected the school and later said that we would be transferred to the primary school."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I heard from the guards that Radovanovic was commander of the 2nd Brigade of the Serb Chetnik army. He also used to beat us, with Todorovic, who often accompanied him. Radovanovic wore a camouflage uniform. He was very tall and very fat, so he was known as Debeli, the fat guy. "Two days after their visit we were transferred to the primary school. At the primary school, there was room in the sports hall, but we had to clean the toilet."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So, Mr. Bicic, will you try and explain to me how come that in 1995 you mentioned the first and last name of the man with the nickname Debeli and now you don't remember that? Was Debeli in fact Srecko Radovanovic; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say yes, though I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But were you sure in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even then I wasn't absolutely sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How frequently did this Radovanovic, Debeli, first name Srecko, beat you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times, together with Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Applying the same methodology when describing the other members of this paramilitary, when you say that Debeli was very tall, what did you really mean? About how many centimetres?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my judgement, he was over two metres in height.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could my learned friend Mr. Krgovic stand up here. Please stand up here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Will you please look at him, Mr. Bicic. And in relation to him, was Debeli taller than he?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And how tall is the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was my intention. Could you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: One ninety-one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: One ninety-one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a clarification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: One --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: One ninety-one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: One nine one. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bicic, how much do you weigh now, roughly?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 110 kilogrammes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In those days this Debeli, who is over 2 metres in height, in relation to your present weight, how much heavier would you say he was?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really tell you how much he weighed, but he was heavy and rather fat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was he heavier than you are today?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, wearing a uniform, as he did, he looked heavier than I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So can we sort of agree that in those days he weighed about 120 kilogrammes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecutor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object at this time. Counsel is not questioning this witness as to any of the testimony that he's given; he's questioning him concerning statements he made in 1995 which were not produced during his direct examination. I don't see any relevance to this. I've let him go for a while, but I just don't see any relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: May I explain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- can explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I would be very glad to explain, Madam President. Firstly, it is my impression that here we have a following situation: Paraphrasing the word of the Honourable Judge May, I would say that the appearances of certain witnesses here is -- might be design, might be called as the testimony by ambush. Because I was checking all the relevant statements of this witness. There is no word of Mr. Blagoje Simic, my client, in all his statements, even the other witnesses. So I was in a situation, firstly, to see this quite detailed expression and description of my client several days before, through this witness, and now I am obliged to go into the centre, into the eye of the storm of this situation. I have to establish all details. Now I have to make a certain reconstruction of these events. Because, as I said, in -- there is not any trace of the mention of my client, and now, out of blue, he mentioned. So that's my situation. I have to establish everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I think I get the point the Defence counsel is making, and he is entitled to cross-examine along those lines, yes. Mr. Pantelic, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So let's finish this question, Mr. Bicic. So we can agree that at that time, Debeli weighed about 120 kilogrammes, if you are saying that he was heavier than you are now?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seemed so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, Mr. Bicic: With whom were you transferred from Bijeljina to Bosanski Samac in mid-May, or, as you said, on the 13th of May, 1992? Of course, I'm referring to the people you knew.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are referring to the people who are detained with me, right? Could you please clarify your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few of us who were taken to Bijeljina were singled out in Bijeljina and taken by helicopter to a place that was unknown to me while the rest were returned with a few more people who were added to our group in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you give me some of the names of some of your fellow citizens who were transferred together with you to the high school in Samac in mid-May? Could you give me names, please?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ibrahim Salkic was transferred, my brother, Dragan Delic, Omer Nalic, Silvestar, Safet Hadzialijagic, Buco; then the people who joined us in Brcko; and I think three or four persons in Bijeljina. I can't remember now. I can't remember all the names. I can mention a few other persons, though, who were taken by helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: There is no need for that, Mr. Bicic. I was interested in the names of these people who came to the secondary school with you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned them. Esad Cosic and, I don't know, all the rest who were there from the very outset together with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So you were with them at the secondary school for a few days; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And together with you, they saw Stevan Todorovic come in with those other persons; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On that day, when Stevan Todorovic came with these other persons -- actually was that the first or the second day of your stay at the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the first day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Approximately at what time did you reach the police station in Bosanski Samac by bus?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. Was it in the morning?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our parts, the morning is until 9.00 a.m., and after that we think that the day already begins. So what time it was, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When did you leave Bijeljina? During the day or during the night?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the day, around 9.00. We didn't have any wristwatches - they had already taken them away from us - so we could not orient ourselves exactly in terms of what time it was exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know approximately how many kilometres there are from Bijeljina to Samac?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Approximately about 80 or 90 kilometres. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you stop anywhere along the road from Bijeljina to Samac?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we stopped somewhere around Loncari, towards Obudovac. That's when the escorts who were escorting us changed. Until then, we were escorted by military policemen from Brcko, those that we met earlier while we were detained at the military barracks. And after that, some persons that I did not know got in. They were wearing police uniforms and camouflage uniforms. I did not know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How long did you stop in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- not in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, in Loncari, in Loncari.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For how long? I don't know. Very briefly until they changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Five, ten, fifteen minutes?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking a lot. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My aim is to ask a lot so that we would clarify the situation.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, and if I were to ask you what you did ten years ago or nine years ago, could you answer me whether you had lunch for 15 minutes or for half an hour or whatever? Not to go into other matters and other problems that I encountered at that time? We were sitting there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel -- I mean Mr. Bicic, please remember that the counsel is asking questions in order to clarify the issues in this trial, and please avoid being rude to him. And, Mr. Pantelic, I think you understand the feelings of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And the fact that time has passed on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bicic, bearing in mind the fact that there was a state of war, can we say that this journey from Bijeljina to Samac by bus lasted for about five or six hours, so that perhaps you arrived in Samac in the early afternoon hours? Would that be correct, in general terms?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That journey was considerably shorter. Let's say it was about two or two and a half hours, to give a rough estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you were transferred to the secondary school, around what time did Stevan Todorovic come together with the rest?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stevan Todorovic, when the bus stopped in front of the police station, he walked out. We saw him through the windshield, that is to say, the front part of the bus, while the other windows had curtains drawn on them. He probably said to these men, these policemen, these soldiers who were escorting us, that they should take us to the gym, to the gymnasium of the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: After that, did he come to the gymnasium with these men when you saw him, when you were describing those events? I mean that afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, let me jog your memory, then. You have just read your statement from 1995, and you say that you were in this gymnasium at the secondary school and that it was not on that day but on the next day that Stevan Todorovic came to that gymnasium with Srecko Radovanovic, Debeli, accompanied by about ten soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me about that day, and I told you that I did not recall that day, but I did see Stevan Todorovic the next day accompanied by Debeli and about ten soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you did say before this Trial Chamber that in that group, there was also Mr. Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the only civilian who appeared in that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On that next day?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Although, you did not mention him in any one of the statements you gave until now.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I probably didn't, but I did see him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Possibly, but none of the people who were there together with you mentioned them [as interpreted] in their statements and no one saw him there. How come?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object. That's not true. That's not true. It's a misleading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Even if it were true, the point is other witnesses were observing other things according to their own condition and their own interests. So, yes, the question has been withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, I would kindly ask the witness to make just a drawing of the gym in secondary school so that we can identify exactly position of the witness, the other persons, and also the other persons that he mentioned, Mr. Todorovic, that person Debeli, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bicic, please take a magic marker. There's a black one over there. I think you can find one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My colleague --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Prior to Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Prior to Mr. Bicic testifying, he made a drawing of the school. If this would be easier for counsel to use this one, which is his drawing -- however, we wind up using Mr. Zecevic's, which was a professional drawing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Was that the secondary school or the primary school?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't believe that's the secondary school. That's the primary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. The primary school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. He --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But, my dear friend, we are speaking about secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The witness can go ahead. It's the gym in the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That was before they went to the primary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. We are in the middle of May. There are two days; firstly, in the gym of secondary school, and then they move on to the primary school gym. So now we are focused on this particular place.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bicic, I think that the other magic marker is better, the one that writes in bold. So please take this magic marker, and could you please draw the layout of the gym and then the entrance, the hallway and the very entrance into the school. Because I really have no idea what all of this is about. Just as you drew the sketch of the TO, just as you drew the sketch of the primary school, and just as you gave very useful instructions to my colleague regarding the sketch of the primary school as compared to the heating plant, et cetera. You know exactly what I'm talking about. So please draw the entrance into this school and the hallway and then the gym.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you perhaps going to pay me a compensation for all these drawings?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that this Tribunal is going to pay you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I can draw this layout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, it's just a rough sketch really. We know that you didn't spend a long time there like the time you spent at the primary school, so it's just a rough sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, Your Honours, for this delay, but I would be very happy if I would have this sketch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's all right, Mr. Pantelic. You know what your client's defence is, so you are entitled to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm thinking about the procedural economy time, you know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but we'll try to have a fair trial as much as we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you put it on the ELMO, please, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Bicic, this is the gym, isn't it, at the secondary school; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You wrote the word "door" up on the top right. Is there a hall that goes from that door?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there is a hall there with locker rooms, something like that. I passed there once as I was entering, and also when I was leaving. I was not really in a position to look around that room because I was rushed on my way in and on my way out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: However, in order to enter the gym, you have to go in through a main entrance, right, into this school, and to go through a hall and then to get to the gym. Could you please draw a very basic sketch for me of that road that you took, so to speak. Or do you simply enter the gym from the street?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. You enter the gym from here, but then also you enter the building from up there, from the workshop of the high school, that is to say, the school yard between the primary school and the secondary school, and then in this direction were the workshops of the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Wait a second. I'll just give you another piece of paper. I would be interested in having a basic sketch as to how you enter the school building, how you reach the gym, and then we are going to explain the gym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But, Mr. Pantelic, I think you are pushing the witness too far. He has explained that he was rushed in and rushed out and he wasn't a resident of that secondary school gym and he was prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And you've heard most of the time they are told not to look up, keep their heads down, and things like that. I think you are pushing the witness too far. Why don't we just go through with questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Like, you can ask him: Where were you standing in relation to when you say whoever you want him to describe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. That would be a better approach. Mr. Usher, could you give me this piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We will mark the rough sketch, though, because it's been looked at. So can we have a number, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Just wait for the number for the rough sketch which is on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number will be D18/1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And it will be ter. It's in Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D18/1 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please use the magic marker to mark with an "X" the place where you were when Stevan Todorovic walked in with the other men. Could you mark that on that drawing, that same drawing.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you have a better pen, that would be easier, because I think it's -- a marker, marker would be better, black marker. Here, Mr. Usher. I have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please mark the "X" that you already marked with this better pen.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is where you were in the gym; right? Thank you. Could you please mark that with the letter "A." Please put the letter "A" there, the letter "A."

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's where you were, Muhamed Bicic, marked with an "A." Could you please give us the position where your brother was, Hasan Bicic.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark his position with the letter "B."

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then who else did you mention? Ibrahim Salkic? Could you please mark his position with the letter "C."

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Who else did you mention? Hadzialijagic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me to do too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. Just the names that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's enough for the witness to say they were all inside the gym. It's enough. Why do you want him to particularise who was standing where? He was not in a position to see that all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but still, there are several persons around him, and I'm going to -- I have intention to cross-examine these coming witnesses on that particular situation, and I want to make a comparation [sic] of their statements. He can say "I cannot remember."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's the very point, because if you force him - which I won't allow anyway - to mark places where he says he's not sure, because of his condition and the passage of time and the way -- the atmosphere in that gym, then you can't hold that against him or even compare to what the other witnesses may draw, because they are bound to be different, so you don't push the witness that far.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So, Witness, if you're unable to mark anybody else's position, don't do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bicic, can you please mark the place where Stevan Todorovic was? So could you please put the letter "X" where Stevan Todorovic was when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, they were standing -- how should I put this? I cannot tell you very precisely now where it was exactly, but let's say it was round the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you mark that with a number "1," please? So Stevan Todorovic, number "1." What about Srecko Radovanovic, Debeli? Could you please mark his position with number "2"? Srecko Radovanovic, number "2."

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please mark the position of Blagoje Simic with number "3"?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Right. So the position of Blagoje Simic is marked with number "3."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you put it on ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bicic, what was Blagoje Simic wearing then?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you give us a bit more detail? Was he wearing a necktie?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you are asking me for too much. I already told you that this was nine and a half years ago and that I cannot remember because I saw the gentleman only once and it was precisely there and it was very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Bicic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, Mr. Bicic, how many times did you have contact with representatives of the Prosecution since the time you gave your last statement in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean when you ask me. You mean here in The Hague? Since I've been in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Before you came to The Hague and also here in The Hague. First tell us before you came to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were you in touch with them several times?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, several times, but I couldn't tell you how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And on those occasions, you didn't make any statements, did you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I made a statement in 1998, if I'm not mistaken, an amendment to my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in that amendment of the 12th of March, 1998, again you didn't mention Blagoje Simic, did you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, as this is not a long statement, it's only one page long, I can give it to you now with the help of the usher. Look through it quickly and see whether you mention Blagoje Simic. Just fly through it.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no wings to fly with. I can only read it. As far as I can see, this mainly relates to Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Turn the page just to make sure, please.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly as I just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Bicic, we can agree, can we not, that in your statement of the 12th of March, 1998, given to the Prosecution, you make no mention whatsoever of Mr. Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this statement, I did not mention him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you about this statement. Please, let's speed things up because my colleague is waiting. Let's move on. My next question, Mr. Bicic: In your statement of 1995, a part of which you just read out, in reference to that specific incident in the secondary school, again you make no mention of Mr. Blagoje Simic, do you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For such a brief visit made by the gentleman who spent a couple of minutes in the hall, I had no intention of mentioning it in my statement, and therefore I saw that gentleman for only a couple of minutes in the secondary school gym, and therefore I thought that a sighting of a couple of minutes was not so important. But as things developed, I saw the gentleman as an accused on photographs, and it was then that I made a statement linked to what I saw, because before, I didn't know that the gentleman was involved to such an extent in the events which occurred in Bosanski Samac and its environs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is a very interesting point. When did you see Blagoje Simic first on photographs as an accused?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in a newspaper. I can't remember when.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But what year was that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I thought you didn't remember the name of the newspaper. Mr. Bicic, you made your statement in February 1995, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in that statement, you mention Stevan Todorovic and Srecko Radovanovic, Debeli, who were in the gym for a couple of minutes and went out with their soldiers, but you did not mention Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just said that I thought it was unimportant, the presence of a civilian, as compared to the presence of men in uniform, whom we feared more than an ordinary civilian, people in civilian clothing. Therefore, I saw the gentleman, Mr. Simic, at the time, together with them, but I have already said that at the time I did not consider that to be of particular importance for me to tell a whole story, to make a story out of those two or three or maybe five minutes that the gentleman spent in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bicic, but you see, you made your statement in February 1995, and then you saw Blagoje Simic you don't remember when. What I'm interested in is when did you decide to mention him in this context? Was it here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned so many things here in The Hague, as well as in other statements earlier on, that I'm really not quite sure when I mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: During your stay here in The Hague, how many times did you meet with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that is the concern of the Prosecution and myself. That is our business. And how many times, I can't tell you. Several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the course of those discussions, did you mention the presence of Blagoje Simic in the gym of the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the same way that I stated here in the courtroom, very briefly for a couple of minutes, and that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether in those days, in 1992, Blagoje Simic had a beard or a moustache when he appeared?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite sincere, let me say, looking closely at Mr. Todorovic, Debeli and those around them, I didn't really take note if somebody had a beard or not, because for us who had been beaten up so badly by those people and to see them again, to look at them could be provoking fate and provoking a repetition of the same. Therefore, please try and avoid reminding me again of those beatings and everything else. Out of fear from all those men, who at any time of day or night could beat us again, to break our bones, it was hard to look at someone straight in the face. It was almost impossible. You could just peep at him, but to really look someone in the face openly would mean to provoke fate as to what would then happen to us. So, please, do not insist on these questions. You have not experienced what we went through.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can we agree, then, that you are not sure that Blagoje Simic was in that group?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm 100 per cent sure that Blagoje Simic was in that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Are you 100 per cent sure that the persons next to Blagoje Simic - and I have in mind in particular Srecko Radovanovic, Debeli - correspond to the descriptions you gave to this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm quite sure that Mr. Todorovic was there, that Debeli or whatever his name was, and a couple of others, maybe up to ten of them. That, I'm sure of.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And are you sure of the physical description?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking too much of me. I've already told you this was nine and a half years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But wait a minute. If it was ten years ago, how can you remember that Blagoje Simic was in civilian clothing? So you do have some memory of it.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blagoje Simic is a citizen of the town I come from and whom I would meet and see often while he was still a boy, who went to school with my brother, and afterwards when he was working as a physician in the health centre in Bosanski Samac, and as a fellow citizen, I would see him frequently in the street. I knew his brother more intimately. So that I know very well who I saw. As for these others who were from elsewhere, I described them through the eyes -- through my own eyes as I saw them then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a second, please? [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bicic. That ends my cross-examination. My colleague, Mr. Zecevic will take over now. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Actually it's not Mr. Zecevic, it's me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Baen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, my name is Catharine Baen, and I am one of the lawyers appointed to represent Mr. Milan Simic in this case. Almost all of the questions I'm going to ask you in order to clarify, I'm going to ask you so that you can answer with a yes or no. An example is -- or a short answer. If I ask you are you wearing a blue-grey jacket today, the answer is either yes or no. It's not, "Yes, and I have on a tie and I always wear this jacket every day," et cetera. The reason why I'm explaining this is we really want this to go quickly. If you want to explain your answer later, Mr. Weiner will get up after I'm through and you can explain everything that needs to be explained. Do you understand this is how cross-examination works?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, you've been a hunter for many years, and I believe we've heard that you were a member of a hunting club; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So it stands to reason you're very knowledgeable about weapons; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hunting weapons, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Is your brother a hunter?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Is he knowledgeable about weapons?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You must ask him that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Well, you have a greater knowledge than he does of weapons, since you're a hunter; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when it comes to hunting weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And you testified that in addition to these legal weapons that Hasan, your brother, had, that he also had these two illegal Kalashnikovs that he bought; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: But he just bought these for himself; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Why did your brother, Hasan, need two Kalashnikovs?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you must ask him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And you and your brother -- you having a greater knowledge of weapons -- you and your brother never discussed the purchase of these two Kalashnikovs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, until the day when the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So you didn't know that he was going to buy these two Kalashnikovs until he had already done it; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And you didn't feel that you needed any more weapons other than the illegal ones you already had; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't need any.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So just the bottom line is: You -- your brother, rather, had two illegal weapons, you had no illegal weapons?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Where was your brother keeping these Kalashnikovs?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably in a part of his own house, that is, our joint house. I lived on the ground floor and my brother lived on the first floor of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. So these guns were kept -- well, let me back up. You've testified that back in April 1992 you and your brother were living in this house together, and you're saying that he was keeping these weapons in that house; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were living together in that house, which had two entrances - and another entrance at the back over the balcony - so that you didn't have to go all the way around the house if I wanted to go and visit my mother and my brother, or my mother to come down and visit me and my wife. So it was linked by a terrace at the back of the house. In fact, it was a house with two separate entrances.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Remember the blue jacket, Mr. Bicic. All I asked you is if you were living in the same house. Okay? And I believe the answer was yes; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Do you understand that possession of an automatic weapon, like a Kalashnikov, was a serious criminal offence at the time under the laws of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You didn't know that it was a serious criminal offence to possess an automatic rifle of this sort?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may explain, then I'll give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: No. I'm just --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if he can just ask [sic] that question and he can explain it fully with Mr. Weiner, we can move fast and we can be done before the lunch break.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Sir, please, do you know whether it's against the law or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: She is using the word "serious criminal offence," and --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'll take "serious" out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- maybe that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Were you aware that it was a criminal offence to possess a weapon of this sort, a Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say no, because I didn't own one.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'm asking of your knowledge of whether or not it was against the law to possess the weapon. I know you said you didn't have one. I'm asking your knowledge of the law, Mr. Bicic. Was it a criminal offence; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A criminal offence was to own illegally all weapons, including a small knife, never mind a rifle. But this was something that didn't interest me, because I didn't have any illegal weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. I understand it doesn't interest you, and you've acknowledged that it is a criminal offence. So did you know that you can go -- for a criminal offence for an illegal weapon, you can go to gaol; right? This really isn't funny. I'm really trying to move this along.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that doesn't interest me. I'm simply telling you I'm not interested, because I did not possess an illegal weapon. You must ask the person who did, if you consider that to be an illegal weapon. I don't know why you are asking me about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, counsel is simply asking you whether you knew, according to the laws at that time in force in the place where you were living, whether it was a criminal offence to own a weapon in the manner that the counsel is asking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I've answered that it was a criminal offence even to have a knife, never mind a firearm. But I don't see why I am being examined about firearms of that kind, as I did not possess an illegal weapon. So I don't see the point of me being asked about it. The person who did possess such a weapon should have been asked that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, when the Trial Chamber is of the view that it's not necessary for you to answer the question, the Trial Chamber will say so; otherwise, please answer the questions asked by counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So I think we can agree, and move on, that you know that it's a criminal offence, or it was back then, to possess this sort of weapon. Did you also understand that under the law at that time in order for it to be a criminal offence, you merely have to possess a weapon; you do not have to own it or have title to it? Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please explain that? I didn't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Possession means actually possessing; it doesn't mean that you own it or have a title to it. If you have it in your possession, then that is a criminal offence.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So you didn't own these Kalashnikovs, but they were in your house; isn't that correct? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in our joint house.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you ever been convicted of possessing any sort of illegal weapon, Mr. Bicic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Have you ever been convicted of any criminal offence?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You've never been convicted of any criminal offence where you were sentenced to gaol time?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Let's turn briefly to talk about April 17th. Now, Mr. Bicic, the month leading up to April 17th, there were armed SDA night patrols, were there not?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You never heard anything about any --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or I'm not aware of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm sorry. You never heard anything in your pizzeria or any of your other establishments about any rumours about any night patrols anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So you never heard anything about any patrols protecting the property of SDA members or you in the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. On April 17th, your brother left your house briefly. Did he go to Prud or the bridge over the river Bosna that day; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Prud or the bridge over the river Bosna on April 17th?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. So when your brother briefly left your house, he went to the centre of town so that he could see what was going on; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. About 50 metres from our house, he passed by our pizzeria and stopped in front of the department store, or the artesian well, around which the citizens of our town had gathered.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And this artesian well, it's -- and I may pronounce this wrong, so correct me - it's called an Arterac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arterac, they called it, yes. Short for artesian well, so they called it Arterac.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I knew I was going to say it wrong. I'm from Texas, and we don't really know how to pronounce the words correctly. This Arterac, it is in the park, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And the mosque is also there in that area in the park too; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Arterac was exactly halfway between the department store and the mosque, in the park.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And there's only one park in the centre of town; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several parks.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So the main park where the Arterac and the mosque are, there's only one park in that area; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is one -- in front of the mosque there was an even larger park, the main park in Samac. To the right of the mosque, there was a smaller park, as far as the SDK building, which is just across the street, across a small street. So there were three parks. One could almost say that they were linked together.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, I'm done with -- I'm at a natural stopping point. I'm going to show him a document now, so I don't know if you want to stop for the break now or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have our break now and resume at 11.30 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Baen, you continue cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, before the break, we were discussing the park, and your final answer right before the break was that these three parks, they were -- "One can almost say they were all linked together"; correct? That's what you just said.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: May I have the usher's assistance with the document, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What document is this?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: This document is entitled, "Decision on measures and proceedings in connection to transfer of orders to conduct mobilisation." Just for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Dated?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: What's the date on it? There is no date on it, Your Honour. Just so you know what is going on with this document, the OTP does have a copy. They've been in possession of this documents since 1998. We just got it from our co-counsels yesterday, and for whatever -- I don't know what reason. But so, therefore, we are requesting an official translation but we can't ask you to take it into evidence right now because we don't have an English translation. So I'm just going to cross-examine the witness with it right now and ask him to read it, and I'm not going to ask it to be admitted since we don't have the official translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. As long as we follow the system where the reading is done slowly, the interpreters can follow, so that we know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can I have confirmation from the Prosecution that they have seen this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We were just given this at the break. There is an indication we've had it since 1998. However, we have no record of this in the system. We have not seen it before today.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic gave it to the OTP with a bunch of other documents in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It was on a list of documents that -- Mr. Pisarevic just gave us a list of documents that have been provided, but we have no record of ever receiving it. We've never seen it before. If he claims he gave it to us, I'm not doubting his word. We've never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can look at it. I know it's in Serbo-Croat. So let me get this clear. Are you intending to produce it at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, only after we get the translation, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The formal English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. So for the purposes of this witness, we will go with it in Serbo-Croat, as long as the passages referring to whatever you want to ask are read out slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour. And should we obtain an ID number at this time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Anything, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. At this point, it would just be introduced for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Right. Can we have a number for identification purposes only?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D4/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Counsel can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, in front of you in Bosnian language are two pages. Now, what I'd like for you to do at this time is read the highlighted portions for the Trial Chamber, but please read slowly for purposes of the interpreters. On the first page, could you please read, at the top of the page, the highlighted portion?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The SDA, the Party of Democratic Action, Bosanski Samac."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And over on the right-hand side of the page, the highlighted portion at the top?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Strictly confidential."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Now, in the middle of the page, there are three highlighted lines. Could you please read those for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Decision on measures and procedures related to conveying orders for carrying out mobilisation."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could you now turn to the second page, and please read the highlighted portion at the top of the second page?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Decision on measures and procedures related to receiving orders on carrying out mobilisation as well as responsible persons for carrying out mobilisation."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could you now read in the middle of the page the highlighted portion?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The park is the location where people are supposed to report Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And could you now read the bottom, right-hand corner of the page and read the highlighted portion?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "President of the SDA of Bosanski Samac, Sulejman Tihic."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I'm finished with this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, let me ask you, when your brother left the house briefly on April 17th to go to the park, did he take his weapons with him, his two Kalashnikovs?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My brother did not go to the park. He was standing in the street between the artesian well and the department store.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Bicic, really, we don't need to argue. My question is: When your brother left the house, did he take his guns with him?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection. That was not her question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see. Yes, I can see, because the question included going to the park, which the witness has explained. Anyway, the part whether he had -- he took the weapons with him, that's what you want to know from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like to know whether the weapons were taken with him.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So it's wartime, it's the peak of the psychosis on April 17th, and these weapons that your brother brought to defend him with, he didn't feel the need to take them with him when he left the house on April 17th; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's argumentative, and they're asking what his brother's thoughts were. He can tell what his thoughts were, but not his brother's.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Baen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The objection is sustained. You've understood what counsel has said.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'll move on. So he didn't take his weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, it has been well established, though, in this trial that by April 1992, many people were arming themselves, legally and illegally, not just your brother; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "legally" and "illegally." Could you please explain that to me a bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'll make the question easier. It's been well established, and you testified to the fact, that many people were arming themselves; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: In fact, not only individuals were arming themselves, but there were some groups that were arming themselves; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And I know you weren't a member, but the SDA, you learned, had formed an armed unit; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You have never heard that the SDA formed an armed unit?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear of the SDA having formed a unit. However, I did hear that it established the Territorial Defence, or rather, that it was the Municipal Assembly, or whoever, that appointed Mr. Fitozovic head of this Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Exactly. And you bring up the name Alija Fitozovic. You never heard a rumour that Alija Fitozovic had put you or your name on a list?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, we've already talked about you being a hunter, and I'm assuming that - and you can tell me if I'm wrong - that a lot of people in Bosanski Samac knew that you were a hunter; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Usher -- actually, the registry. I tried to inform you of this during the break. We'd like to present the witness with document D, as in "David," 17/1 ter. Yes, Mr. Usher. Thank you. Could you please put the -- if you haven't already, put the Bosnian version in front of the witness and the English version on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, could you please take a look at the document in front of you and tell me, do you see your name on this list?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, the penultimate name. It says "reserve," and then underneath that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And the number next to it, 62-607, was that your telephone number in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've forgotten. I really can't say, because we had three or four telephone numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. So you don't remember whether that was your telephone number. Do you recognise -- well, first of all, before I go any further, could you read the top of the page, what the title of this document is?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Hunters' Section," "K.dir," probably "Jasarevic, Hasan."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Take a look at the document. Do you recognise any of the other names on this list?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: What names do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the names that are here. I know all these men.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Were any of these men members of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the answer to that, but I can say that Dzevad Seljakovic was in the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You know all the people on this list, and you have no idea if any of them were members of the SDA; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Not one?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Are any of the people on this list, were they a member of the hunting club with you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All of them were members of the hunting club.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So all the members on this list were known hunters?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Are all the individuals on this list Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Were any of these people on this list in detention with you at any time?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Which ones?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pasaga Tihic, Dzevad Jusufovic, who was released immediately, a day or two later. He was released from the Territorial Defence building.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, for purposes of just the record, could he just read out the number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you, but just so -- it's hard for me to follow the names. Mr. Bicic, I'm sorry; could you mention the number and then the name, please.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1; number 2, but number 2 was there only for a day or two. I cannot say for sure. He was released after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And please, the number and the name, sir, please.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dzevad Jusufovic, number 2; number 6, Dzevad Seljakovic; and on the reserve force, Avdo Drljacic, number 2 -- I beg your pardon. Number 6, Dzevad Seljakovic. Not Dzevad Seljakovic; his brother. I made a mistake there. His nickname was Mrki, but Dzevad was not detained. Also, this Mrki, his brother who was there, he was released a day or two later.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Is that all -- excuse me, are those all the persons who were in detention with you on the list? Have you named all of them now?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm done with that document, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, have you ever seen that document before?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: No one's ever shown it to you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Bicic, I'd now like to direct your attention to the period of your detention in the primary school. But before I do that, let me just ask you one thing: You testified that during your entire stay in detention, you saw Milan Simic only twice; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Just the one time he came to beat and then the five to seven days later when he came back. Okay. We are now in the primary school. I want to direct our attention there. And several days ago, I think October 26th, you testified about the position of the detainees in the gym hall at the primary school. Mr. Weiner had you go through and you said that you were able to recall seven different individuals and their position -- excuse me, I've been corrected by my co-counsel.
