Eight people in the gym hall and their position. We have taken the same diagram that Mr. Zecevic made and provided to Mr. Weiner and we have put in the positions for eight people, and we are going to ask you, for purposes of the record now, to point those out and so I could --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: If I could have the assistance again, Mr. Usher. I'm keeping you busy. But if you could take this diagram to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. You have the Bosnian version in front of you, which we've enlarged a little bit. We've got the English version on the ELMO. And with Mr. Zecevic's expertise on these drawings, he's added the boiler room, the workshop, and the windows that you described that start halfway up on the wall of the entrance hall. Okay? Could you take a look at that document now, Mr. Bicic. Okay. You talked about the positioning of the eight detainees in the gym hall, and I'm now -- I've numbered the -- or I haven't numbered. Mr. Zecevic numbered the eight positions. And just to clarify the record, or supplement Mr. Weiner's examination, I'd like for you to identify on the diagram where exactly the detainees were positioned. And we'll just start with position number "1," and you just tell me the name of the person, and then we'll go that way. Okay? So who was positioned in position number "1," Mr. Bicic? Isn't it -- that's Silvestar Antunovic; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I've already said - and I can point it out here - that in this part and in this part here, that's where we were, as far as I could remember, from the door and down the gym. So here, where number "8" is, it was not that there was one person there; there were four or five persons there. And then further on, the rest.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. Then what I'll have you do is get a pen or the thin marker from the usher and you can place the numbers where they belong, to make sure it's completely accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I don't think it's fair to ask the witness to be completely accurate, because we've been through this problem before.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: What I mean, Your Honour, is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: As far as he can remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: On page 31, lines 2 through 10 -- actually, it's page 2986 of the transcript on the 26th, he went through and said he was able to remember the position of each one of them. So I went back and looked at it because I know Your Honour's position on this, so it's in the transcript he knows where they were. So what I'm saying is to be accurate -- I mean, we made a mistake. I can't believe Mr. Zecevic made a mistake, because he never makes mistakes, but we made a mistake on this diagram. So I thought it would be fair to the witness to let him put the numbers where they belong and he can discard or he can cross out our mistakes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, then could you please put a number "1" where Silvestar Antunovic was positioned.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: On the ELMO, yes, please. Okay. Not working? Do you have another copy? Okay. Have you marked number 1?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could he not write on the ELMO? Is it a problem? Could he write on the ELMO the numbers? No? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could you mark number "2" the position where you were located.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could you now mark a number "3" where your brother Hasan was located.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could you mark a number "4" where Ibrahim Salkic was located.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could you mark a number "5" where Buco was located.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And by the way, this Buco, I understand, is a nickname. Could you tell me what this person's full name is, Mr. Bicic, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nurkic. I can't remember his first name.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Could you mark a number "6" where Safet Hadzialijagic was located.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could you mark a number "7" where Dragan Delic was located.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could you mark a number "8" where Omer Nalic was located.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could we now place that on the ELMO, please? And for purposes of the record, Your Honour, could it be indicated that the witness has placed the eight indications on the diagram, just so that the record reflects that he complied?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So Mr. Bicic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And before -- this is a clean copy, isn't it, the one you've given him to mark?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And can we have it numbered in the same group with the original one, so that we don't get confused? I'm sure it will have a slash.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Counsel, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, so this diagram accurately reflects the position of these eight detainees; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So you are next to your brother and Ibrahim Salkic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: If you could take another look at this diagram, in the middle of the page, where the -- there are four squares that have the letters, "A," "B," "C" and "D" on it. If you could take a look at the diagram and locate that? You testified earlier that you, your brother, Perica Misic, and Ibrahim Salkic were lined up against the wall opposite the entrance hall during the incident with Milan Simic -- the entrance, yeah, opposite the entrance during the incident with Milan Simic. Now, if you could please tell me who is in position "A" and "B" and "C" and "D." Let's start with "A". Who was in position "A"?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. In position "A" was Perica Misic for a while. Then my brother, me, Ibrahim Salkic. However --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'll let you explain --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, please, I haven't finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let the witness answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Go ahead. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, as this beating went on, we often shifted positions. As they were beating us, they were moving us from one place to another, so I'm no longer sure after a few minutes where which person was, because they were shooting above our heads into the glass pane that was facing the heating plant. So during this beating, our positions changed. It's not that we wanted to change our positions, but they were kicking us, beating us, and that simply led to us being moved from one position to another.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. I understand. It's fair enough that you didn't stay in this position. Let me make it more clear, then. When you first came in, the position that you just testified to, that was their position; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, what was the distance between you and the others when you first came in this area for the beating?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the persons that were detained like me, or are you referring to the persons who were beating us and shooting and I don't know what all?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Right. I'm told by my co-counsel I haven't made this clear. You said that position "A" was Perica Misic; position "B" was your brother. Who was in "C" and "D" when you first came out there in the hall?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I and Salkic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Who was position "C"? I need to know exactly which position. That's what's not being made clear, and it's probably my fault. Who was in position "C," you or Salkic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said I, and then Salkic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I know, but who was in position "C," position "C"? Either you or Salkic is in one position "C."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think the witness is following the sequence of the letters; himself in "C" and Salkic in "D."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I just wanted to make sure the record was clear, Your Honour. I understand that's probably what he's saying, but I want to make sure the record properly reflects it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: If you could just say who was in position "C." Give me the name.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant it was -- I thought it was sufficient, if I said "I," that I was referring to myself. You know my name, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes. And then in position "D," who is in position "D"?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ibrahim Salkic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the distance between the four of you - Ibrahim Salkic and you and Perica and your brother - when you first came into this area, what was the distance between you as you were lined up?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ten, twenty centimetres at the most.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let me ask you another thing about this area where you were standing, this entrance hall. What is the distance between the entrance door to the primary school and the wall where you four were lined up?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 3 metres; 2 and a half, 3 metres. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Bicic, you testified that you were all lined up there and that Milan Simic starts waving his gun around. Could you please show the Trial Chamber what you mean by "waving his gun around"?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the Court's permission, could he demonstrate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the witness can.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was holding his pistol. It was a small automatic pistol. He moved it from one to the other, pointing it in our direction. Then he fired, I think, two shots.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: What I'm asking you to do, just for the Trial Chamber, is to show him -- show exactly his motions with the gun. When you say he was waving it around, show the Trial Chamber how he was waving it around, exactly how he did it.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was pointing it at each one of us and then going back.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. So for the purposes of the record, Your Honour, could the record show that the witness had a magic marker in his right hand and was waving it in front of him, back and forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, as counsel pleases.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, you mentioned this weapon that Mr. Simic had in his hand, Mr. Milan Simic, and you said earlier it was a Scorpion. Can you describe in detail about this gun, for example, the length of the barrel, this sort of information, just so the Court can visualise the size of the weapon and what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was in the army, this pistol, or small automatic gun, as they called it, a Scorpio, was carried only by officers of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'm just asking for a description of the gun, actually. Not a history of the gun, but a physical description of the weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, if you know. If you don't know, you say so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know, yes. It was about 30, 35 centimetres long. I'm not quite sure about its length, because I never held it in my hand. It had an extension made of wire which made it into like the butt of the pistol. I know that it could fire individual shots and also bursts of fire. I know this from the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And does it have something underneath the barrel for your free hand to grab so that you can aim with it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think below the barrel you would put in the ammunition clip.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Bicic, could you point out on the diagram on the ELMO, with the pointer you have, where Milan Simic was standing when he was waving this gun in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Simic was here, at the very entrance. This is where the door was. There was a window on one side of the door and another window on the other side of the door.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. May the record reflect the witness has complied with that request, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So Mr. Simic was waving this gun around, and you said that - I don't think it was clear in the testimony the other day - there were several shots, but you're saying today there were two shots. Is that what you're saying today, Mr. Bicic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said two or more. I don't know. I'm not sure. Because of the fear, I don't know whether there were more.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. So there were at least two shots; there could have been more. Do you understand -- are you sure there was only one shot, because -- I mean more than two shots? Because we've heard testimony there was just one shot. You're saying there's either two or more. You're sure? You're positive there was two or more shots?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am positive.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You testified that the shots went between, between, the heads of you and your brother; correct? That was your testimony back last Friday, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they flew through the glass of the window. Because halfway up were bricks, and from then on there were windows of this heating plant, so that the glass panes shattered and the glass fell on us.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. So all of the shots went between you and your brother and went through the glass, as you just described. So if there was testimony that there was only one shot and it went directly above your brother's head, that would not be correct, would it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Baen, you've got the background of this witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And in that situation, each one of them observed whatever they could and heard whatever they could.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I know that, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you can't say -- you can't put the evidence of another witness and challenge his or the other witness's.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Maybe I went about it the wrong way. I understand what you're saying. But, Your Honour, it's extremely proper in cross-examination to go over the inconsistencies in the testimony. If I did it the wrong way, I apologise to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, it's generally correct, but not in this case, in this situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You know why, because of the evidence that the witness has given as to what was happening to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, you testified that after these gunshots, someone ordered the four of you to put your hands behind your heads and to stand up against the wall; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before that, when the shooting stopped, they started beating us. And during the beating, they showed us and ordered us the way we should stand. It was not just an order; it was through the beatings we were positioned in the way I showed here in this courtroom when I was testifying.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Right. Okay. So as you're put in this -- or after you're put in this position, you said that then Mr. Simic aimed his boot at you, he aimed at your genitals, was your testimony, and he kicked -- at that point he kicked each one of you in the genitals; isn't that correct? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And where was he standing - if you could please show on the diagram - when he kicked you? Point out where you are, and then point out where he is. Okay. Point out where you are first.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: In the position number -- letter "C."

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, in the process of the beating, before they leaned us against the wall, I no longer knew who was where. We were simply there. I didn't dare look around, out of fear. We were standing more or less in a line there, whereas Mr. Simic, with his escort, was all around us. We were surrounded. Behind us were the broken glass windows. We were standing there, with our legs spread apart, our hands behind our heads. And then this gentleman, from a distance of 1 or 2 metres - I can't say exactly - ran up to us and hit us with his boot in our genitals.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Let me try to do a better job of going back to the yes-and-no questions. Was Mr. Simic, when he kicked you, was he standing right in front of you; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the Court's permission, can we have the witness stand and show how Mr. Simic kicked, the kicking motion, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What's the point of all this?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: How he kicked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What's the point of this?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: To show whether it was a front, forward motion or whether it was side by side or whether it was from behind him, just to show exactly how, as he was standing there, the defendant kicked him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What is the point of this?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: The point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is the point of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: To supplement his testimony or to clarify exactly how he was kicked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't think it's necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You're denying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't think it's necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So you're denying my request to have the witness demonstrate the kick?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. May I ask him questions, of course, about it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, when Mr. Milan Simic was standing in front of you and he kicked you, did he kick you in a straightforward motion, from down to up?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was, as I was saying, about a metre and a half away from me, something like that, so he made a step with his left foot and kicked me with his right foot, directly in the area of the genitals. However, I noticed this, so I bent down a little so that I received one of those blows above my genitals.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While -- I'd like to clarify everything, because this wasn't just one blow. There were two or three blows, whereas these blows were falling mostly in the area of my stomach and thighs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. So he kicked you. He was standing right in front of you, and you said he kicked you three times is what you testified to the other day; isn't that correct? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And all three times he missed your genitals; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not absolutely. Once he hit my thigh, but partly my genitals as well, as I said, and then another time. Was it the first or the second, I can't say now. I can't ascertain with certainty which was the first time, which was the second. When I bent down, I leaned forward and so I got the third blow in my stomach, which means that one of the first two blows did hit me partly in my genitals and partly in my upper leg or thigh.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, you testified last October 26, your quote -- just as a quote, "Luckily, he hit me above my sex organs." So what I'm asking you is all three times he kicked you, he hit you above your sex organs. You didn't mention anything last Friday about him hitting your genitals, did you? If you want to revise that now to clarify, then that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying luckily, on that occasion, I can say that he didn't hit me on my genitals.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So then he did later?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was later he hit my right thigh and partly my genitals, but the strength of that blow was probably much smaller than the time he hit me and caused a large swelling the size of a fist.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: We know about your medical problems. I'm just asking about where he kicked you, to clarify it, on every single kick. So you're saying on each kick -- well, the first one he missed, and then you're saying the second one he hit your thigh and your genitals; that's correct? And we can move on if that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. So you stated that after you were released, that you talked to some of your friends, and because of your medical problem, you went to see a doctor or a specialist; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Do you remember the doctor's name or where his office was?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That doctor used to work in Slavonski Brod in the general hospital there. What his name was, I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember the names of any of the friends you talked to who suggested you go to this specialist?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My brother, and his friend Pero, and the brother of this Pero.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. And have you seen any doctors for this problem since you saw the specialist?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, shortly after that, about some 20 days later, I was transferred to Istria, where my mother, wife, and daughter were. They were accommodated there. And I met a surgeon there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name was Sinisa. I can't remember his surname now. Unfortunately, he died a couple of years ago from cancer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Simic, moving on -- or we are trying to close this topic or I am -- excuse me, Mr. Bicic, Mr. Simic, you said, kicked you, at least several times, and while he did this, he had his Scorpion in one hand and he had an iron bar in the other hand; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So he had the gun in his right hand and he had the bar in his left hand; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Well, so it was the opposite? The gun was in his left hand and the bar was in his right hand?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, yes, because he switched his pistol to his left hand and one of his escorts gave him the bar, which he held in his right hand.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Can you show the Chamber how he held these two items in his hand when he kicked you - just sitting there - to show how he held them when he kicked you? The pointer can be the bar and the marker can be the gun, the Scorpion.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In his left hand he held, like that, downward, the Scorpion, and in his right hand, roughly in this position, turned upwards, with his arm raised, he was holding the bar.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So one arm was raised and the other one was down? The one with the bar in it was down; is that correct? Excuse me, the opposite. The hand with the gun was down, and the hand with the bar was up; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And while he was doing all of this stuff to you four, these beatings and kickings, did you ever have any idea that he might be drunk?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me too much. I was afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'm just asking you, yes or no, if you had any idea he was drunk. If the answer is no, then it's no. If you were afraid and -- I understand if you're afraid and you therefore you didn't notice whether he was drunk, then it's -- no is fine.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can answer by saying I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. After the beatings, you were brought back to the gym hall and Milan and escorts left, and you said that five to seven days later, Milan returned to the -- Milan Simic returned to the school. So I want to direct your attention to this second incident. You testified that Milan, your brother, and Perica Misic were gone for several hours that night; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And you were worried while they were gone, but when your brother and Perica Misic returned, your brother told you what happened. He told you that Milan was -- he gave them food; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My brother told me that Milan came with the intention of apologising to my brother, to Perica, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you'll just answer the question I asked you, we'll get there, we will move through this quickly and we will be done by lunch. Okay. He gave them food and they also drank beer, didn't they? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what my brother told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Right. And he was nice to them, your brother told you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on that occasion he was nice.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And your brother also told you that they had friendly conversation; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And your brother also told you that Milan Simic had heard that your brother would be exchanged; isn't that correct? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would answer differently, if I may, not just with a yes or a no.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... okay. Mr. Weiner, I promise you, will give you a chance to fully explain, but what I'm asking you right now - and it is yes or no - did your brother tell you that he was going to be exchanged, that he was told that he was going to be exchanged; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And Mr. Simic apologised, as you started to explain earlier, he apologised to your brother and Perica; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So Milan Simic beat the four of you, but he only apologised to Perica Misic and your brother Hasan Bicic; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Don't you think that's sort of strange?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: He can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: She is asking this witness whether he thinks Milan Simic's conduct is strange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. His own impression of what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the witness can answer that.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question once again?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Milan Simic beat the four of you, but he only came to apologise to your brother and Perica Misic. Don't you think that that is strange? He didn't apologise to you; he didn't apologise to your friend Ibrahim Salkic.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally not, but he said to my brother and Perica that he apologised to us too.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Let's talk about Ibrahim Salkic. He's a very good friend of yours and your brother's; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And he goes by the nickname Ibela?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: How long have you and Ibela been friends?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, practically from early childhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And he's your best friend; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Was he ever good friends with Milan Simic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. However, since Mr. Simic often came to our pizzeria, Ibela also often came to the pizzeria and they would always stand by the bar. They would usually be in that standing area. How friendly they were, I don't know, but they would talk.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sure they talked. It was a small town. I'm from a small town, and I understand how everybody knows everybody. My question is: Were they good friends, like you and Ibela? Milan Simic and Ibela, were they good friends, close, intimate friends?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that they were not that close, intimate friends.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Did they work together?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Well, he's your best -- Ibela is your best friend. You never heard that he and Milan Simic worked together?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I heard that Perica, while he was president of the municipality, and Milan, who also did something at the municipality, that they worked together in a way. I don't know. But I don't know about Ibela and Simic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. How often did you and Ibela see each other and talk to each other before the events of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that period, not that often because I was very busy with my restaurants and the machines that were rented out in our municipality and in the neighbourhood, so often I had to go out with repairmen to have these machines repaired, serviced.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Bicic. I understand you were very busy. My question is: How often did you see him? And you said not so often; okay? Is that correct? We can just keep moving.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not that often.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. And then you were detained together, you've testified, and positioned next to each other in the gym hall of the primary school, and then you were released the first part of September, and sometime thereafter Ibela was released. After you were both released, how often did you and Ibela talk to each other?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that period, when I was exchanged, for a while I was in Istria and then I went to Germany with my family. That's where I live now as well. A few years later Ibela got in touch with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also when he came to Germany. So we lived in two different towns about 600 kilometres away from each other, perhaps even more than that. So in that period we could see each other only when he was in transit, when he was travelling to Bosnia. That would be for a few hours, in order to get a rest, to get something to eat, and then he would continue. That is to say, that in the period starting with our exchange, or rather, my exchange, until that period when Ibela left Germany, we met two or three times, but, as I said, only briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have an occasion to -- so you did see him, Ibela, the first year or two after he was exchanged in Germany. Let me ask you this: You're aware that your best friend has made a couple of formal statements to the Office of the Prosecutor, are you not?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: In fact, he made one in February, the same -- 1995, the same month as you, and then he also made one during the same time period as you and your brother, in Germany, in March 1998; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Did your brother make a statement in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Let me ask you about this March 1998 statement. Where was this conducted, the taking of your statement in March 1998?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My statement was taken in my apartment in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Who was there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who I gave the statement to were present.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Who were those persons you gave the statement to?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the names.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: How many individuals were there from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think three, three persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And I see on the front of your statement that there it says --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: It says at the bottom, on the front of your statement, "Names of all persons present during the interview," and there's been a redacted name. It shows that there was an interview, Tore Soldal, interpreter Tanja Novak, and then there's a name redacted at the bottom. Do you have any idea who that might have been who was present, whose name was redacted?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So you were -- so your brother was living in the same place as you at that time, Germany; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't live there. At that time he came to visit our mother and me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: That's right. He came to visit you and your mom. All right. You were aware that Milan Simic voluntarily surrendered in February, late February 1998, isn't that correct, right before you gave your statement?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And immediately thereafter, the OTP, Office of the Prosecutor, contacted you and your brother, asking that you add some information about Milan Simic; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Office of the Prosecutor contacted me in order for me to provide details about Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Exactly. Okay. I want to talk to you -- and I'm going to try to move this along, if you can help me. Mr. Pantelic has talked a lot about your 1995 statement, and I want to ask you a couple of questions about it too, but I want to try to move through how the statement was taken, for purposes of the record, to show that it was voluntary.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: If I could have the usher's assistance in presenting the statement to the witness, I'd appreciate it, the 1995 statement. We have it right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: They haven't been produced.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: No, we haven't provided them. We've got them here. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. -- they are with counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could these at least be marked for identification, because we're constantly referring to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let me clarify that with counsel. These are the two statements recorded by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: This is the 1995 statement that Mr. Pantelic was talking about. There's only one 1995 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So that's the one you are -- you want to discuss?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Exactly. We're not offering it into evidence; we're just cross-examining him with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. There is no harm in having them marked for identification. Then they can be kept by the Registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So we can just refer to them. I'm not asking that they be placed in evidence either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the number for the 1995 statement made by the witness to the Office of the Prosecutor, just for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D5/2 ter ID, and D5/2, for the English, ID.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, you have --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: If you could put the English on the ELMO and then the Bosnian in front of him, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, you have a document in front of you. There's an English version on the ELMO. I've given you the Bosnian version that you can more easily follow the questions. If you need your glasses, please, you can go ahead and put them on. I would like for you to look at the front page. Across the top it says "ICTY," or "International Criminal Tribunal for the prosecution of persons responsible for serious violations of international law committed in the territory of the former Yugoslavia since 1991." It does say that at the top of the page, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one thing: I forgot my glasses at home. I haven't brought them at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You can't read anything? We requested --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read, but you said that I should put my glasses on, and I was just trying to say that I can't put them on because they're not here.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Well, thank you. I wasn't ordering you to put your glasses on; just if you needed them, it was permissible. Okay. Thank you. In the middle of the page, it says "witness statement," and then also down in the middle of the page it has the dates of the interview, February 22nd through the 24th, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this as your statement? Take a look at it if you need to. On the front page, you'll see, of the English version, at the bottom right, it's been signed and initialed. If you want to look at the English version also and identify your signature, please, sir. Is this your statement and is that your signature and initials, on the English version?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: If you'll flip through the English version, you can see that each page is initialed, please. And I ask you if you accept those as your initials.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: If you turn to the last page of the statement, the witness acknowledgement, it's dated February 24th, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And you signed this acknowledgement on that date and you accept that this signature is yours; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: It's the next page. There's one other page after that, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we make sure that we have the same number of pages?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes. I want to make sure - excuse me - that we have the right -- I have the witness acknowledgement. I don't know why it's -- if we can supplement the acknowledgement, make sure he can identify that as his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Up here, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could you please put it on the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Now, it's also true that this statement you made, you made it voluntarily and you told the truth; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: No pressure was put on you, and you spoke freely and you were not hurried; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody rushed me, and I gave the statement voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And you spent three days with these investigators: the 22nd, the 23rd, and the 24th of February, 1995. Could you please tell me how many hours you spent on all three of those days, roughly, because I know this was a while ago. Day one, how many hours did you spend?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Was it one hour, or was it more like four or five hours, six or seven? Just a general idea. I know it was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, something like that. Well, let's say four or five hours perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And was it like that also on day two and day three, four or five hours?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, something like that. Sometimes a bit less. Around that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And this statement was made about three years after the events of 1992, and these events were fresher in your mind, obviously, back then; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fresher. But giving these statements, just like now, answering these questions, either yours or from the gentleman from the other side, do remind a person and make him a bit nervous. Going back to that period is not really easy, re-experiencing all these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I understand. Your statement was approximately 13 pages long and full of detail; isn't that correct? Look to see how many pages there are to confirm that, please. The statement is in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Baen, I'm wondering why we are going in these minute details, because you asked him to identify his signatures on all the pages, which he did. Why should we go --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'm following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- talking pages and all that?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we go to the salient points?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I have two more questions for the foundation. I'm trying to follow the law of -- common law of the United States and also here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. We -- yes, we normally don't do that here, because we don't want to keep the witnesses in the box unnecessarily too long.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So he has identified his signature. You move along to what points you want to make out of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: We'll move on. If he could just answer the last question, then I'll gladly move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Then proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, if you look at the statement, it's 13 pages long?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Baen --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I thought he could answer the last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Oh, he can't?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He is not answering about the number of pages. I've told you that is not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. I misunderstood, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I hope so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, could you please turn to -- in the Bosnian version, could you turn to page 9, the last paragraph, the last sentence, the last --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: -- where the beginning of the sentence says, "He came," referring to Milan Simic. Could you start reading there, and read --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And also in the English, the English version, Your Honour, it's page 9 of this statement, the last paragraph, the second sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, have you located in the Bosnian version where it says -- talks about Milan Simic, 34, black hair, tall, slender, and he would come to the camp? If you could start reading there and read that sentence out loud for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "He would come to the camp with his bodyguards in mid-June, and called out me, my brother, and Perica Misic. He took us to a corridor between the sports hall and the burnt area, where he severely beat us, together with his bodyguards."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could you go ahead and read the next two sentences out loud for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which sentences do you mean actually?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: The next sentence after the one you just read.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "After that beating, I could not urinate for days, and the area above my genitals was swollen as big as a fist." Should I go on reading?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: The next sentence, please. Read the next sentence.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "It healed when I got out of camp."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. So you stated in your statement in 1995 that only you, your brother, and Perica Misic were beaten by Milan Simic on that one occasion in the primary school; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You did not say anything about Ibrahim Salkic being beaten by Milan Simic on that occasion or any other occasion; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably didn't say on that occasion. I don't know why. And then after all of that, perhaps it was the interview itself that reminded me of the pain that was still fresh in my mind and the other events. I just -- I just omitted to mention Salkic in all of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. My question - yes or no - you omitted, didn't mention, anywhere your best friend, Ibrahim Salkic, in your statement in 1995? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I omitted to mention him here.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And the OTP never heard anything from you about Ibrahim Salkic being beaten until you gave your statement in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I was just taking it in and wondering how the witness could know that the OTP had never heard that, whether it included even from other people, other witnesses, which is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I can leave it at that, you didn't mention it in your 1995 statement, and move on to one more topic and then we are done. Mr. Bicic, you're involved in a lawsuit in the United States, are you not?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And this lawsuit you and several others have filed against a person named Nikola Vukovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes. You can go, please. The usher, you can go. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And Kemal Mesinovic, who lives in the United States, contacted you in early 1998 to let you know he was filing this lawsuit to recover money and asked if you would join him, and you joined in the lawsuit in September 1999; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Kemal Mesinovic addressed me with a request as to whether I would be willing to testify that Vukovic, who altered his documents so that he was now called Nikolic and then managed to get to Germany with these false papers -- I'm sorry, to the United States - that's what I meant - that's where they recognised him. That's where he was recognised by persons who were also in camps. And they accused him of the crimes that he committed in those camps. Miki was his nickname. So I mentioned him in the statement as Miki.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: My question: Did you join in the lawsuit; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I joined in the sense of testifying against him, not being familiar with the laws of the United States, namely that thereby I became one of the parties that was filing the lawsuit. However, I mostly talked to people who came to see me through some unofficial interpreters. I talked to them in the German language, and my German is not all that good -- or interpretation from German into English -- or, rather, from English into German was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I don't want to cut him off. I just asked - yes or no - did he join the lawsuit, and then I was going to present --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He just wanted to make it clear in what capacity, because, as he said, he didn't know the U.S.A. laws.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I understand that, but he did confirm what I was trying to get him to confirm, that he did become a party, in his answer, and I have the petition here with his name as a party also. I understand it's not in his language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is the point of all this?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Right now, Your Honour, I'd like to offer, because it's proper under Rule 94 for purposes of judicial notice, that you take judicial notice of the formal complaint that is filed in the United States District Court in Georgia where four different people filed a lawsuit against Mr. Vukovic, including Mr. Bicic, and that he testified in that trial last week, and it's proper that you take judicial notice, and I'd like to offer the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What for? I know we can take judicial notice, but what for? What's the relevance in this case?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Because -- are you going to take judicial notice? Are you telling me you will take judicial notice of the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I want to know the relevance.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: The relevance is there are 33 pages full of detail at the primary school of all the beatings, including Vukovic and others, and nowhere in that document is Mr. Milan Simic mentioned, the whole time he was at the primary school. And that's it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So are you -- will you take judicial notice under Rule 94? And then I have two more questions, and I'm done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. That is evidence which you say was given in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It's not the evidence. It is the official document that is filed in the U.S. district court by this man and three other plaintiffs, which was given to me by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. So it's the formal complaint?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes. It is a formal, official court document, which is the formal complaint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Unless we have a copy of it --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: We have all the copies ready. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would just want to clarify. It is not a statement of this witness. It's the complaint, which -- the case was initiated, not by this witness, by someone else in another country, strictly a complaint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because I wanted more clarification about that. Usually, if it's a formal complaint, obviously it must have been drawn out -- drawn up by an attorney.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In which case, it's not the statement of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: It is not a statement. It is a formal court document that's been sworn and filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then we don't need it, because you can only attack him on his own statement. We don't need that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I was just asking the Court to take judicial notice of the document. I wasn't going to be cross-examining him on it. If that's the Court's position, that you don't want to take judicial notice, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's not relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: He testified about the beatings at the primary school, Your Honour. I think it's very relevant, respectfully, to -- for purposes of my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Anything else, Mr. Prosecutor? Anything else? Did you want to comment on what counsel said?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I was going to say, if it's testimony, if they want to use it, that's one thing. But this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There is no harm in bringing it to the attention of the Trial Chamber. There is no problem taking judicial notice, except that I'm saying it may not be relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: That's perfect. And I see it's past 1.00. But that does raise an issue. His testimony has been requested -- Mr. Bicic's testimony, I'm told, in the United States, has been requested by the Office of the Prosecutor, and us as well, the day that he testified. It won't be ready, the court reporter said, until Friday. So I don't think we are going to have any questions for him, but I just wanted to put on the record that we had requested it and it won't be ready until Friday, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can -- for your own purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You are through with cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I have maybe a couple more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's after 1.00, so we will resume at 15.30 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Yeah. Thank you. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.05 p.m. 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Baen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. At this time we would like to provide the Chamber with this petition that we're talking about in the lawsuit that this witness and three other persons filed in the United States regarding the events at the primary school, and I believe the Court had agreed to take judicial notice, I believe, and so we're providing the documents at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution is on their feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no objection to taking judicial notice that there is, in fact, a lawsuit in the United States, that he is part of this lawsuit. However, the information within the complaint doesn't fall under Rule 94 for judicial notice. Judicial notice, Rule 94, section A, says: "A Trial Chamber shall not require proof of facts of common knowledge but shall take judicial notice thereof." In paragraph B, the Court further states, in its pertinent part: "After hearing the parties, the Court may decide to take judicial notice of adjudicated facts or documentary evidence from other proceedings of the Tribunal relating to matters" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry -- "may take judicial notice of adjudicated facts or documentary evidence from other proceedings of the Tribunal relating to matters at issue in the current proceedings."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: To take judicial notice of all the facts in that statement of facts and the complaint really becomes a 94 bis type situation, where you're trying to submit evidence as opposed to utilise witness testimony. With regard to the fact that he is part of a suit, they filed suit, we have no problem taking judicial notice of that. But however many pages that complaint is, that information, I think, is beyond the Rule of judicial notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. This is why I was asking counsel, because I'm sure Ms. Baen has read these Rules and she knows what it is limited to.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I do. And if I may respond, for purpose of the record, Your Honour, I'm not referring -- I've read Rule 94 and the rest of the Rules many times here in the Tribunal. I'm not referring to the latter part of the Rule. I'm referring to -- which deals with proceedings, taking judicial notice of proceedings in Court, proceedings here. I'm talking about the first part of the Rule that talks about "common knowledge," and certainly an official document that is filed in a federal district court in the United States of America is something that could be considered to be common knowledge. You can find it on the Internet, for example. I mean, the whole world -- this is an official document filed by this witness and three other persons, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The point is, we did understand how the witness came into this, and he has explained, and as far as the Trial Chamber is concerned, it really doesn't matter what proceedings are going on in that other country and what they are about and what the focus is really.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: The focus is what happened at the primary school, which is exactly what we're focused on for our client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. Because those are different proceedings. Are they criminal proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: No. They're just like - I hate to use an example - just like O.J. Simpson. There's a criminal case arising out of the same -- there's a civil case and a criminal case arising out of the same facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, I don't agree. Whatever the purpose is, you can introduce your documents, but we are all agreed that we are aware that these are proceedings taking place in whatever country and whatever -- for whatever purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So you're denying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We acknowledge that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. So you're denying admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. You can have them admitted, for whatever they are worth, but they are not relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. That's all I'm asking for, is that they be admitted into evidence. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Once again, we just object to that, because those facts -- the allegations in that are not part of the common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I see the point you are making. I know what the Rules mean. I see the point the Defence counsel is making, and I'm sure they've seen that as far as the Trial Chamber is concerned as to what they will do with those documents, how much weight to attach to them, is a matter that I'm sure the Defence counsel is aware from the discussions that we've been going through.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And I wouldn't like the witness to think that what was said there would have an effect on these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: We would too, Your Honour. Mr. Bicic -- here are the documents. Would the usher take the documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If I may ask, Ms. Baen, these proceedings are still going on?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, they are not going on. What happened was -- and I've talked to all the lawyers involved in this lawsuit; I'm very familiar with what's going on. There is testimony last Monday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. My question is: Are they still going on? Are they completed?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Well, that's a tricky question because the defendant did not show up for trial, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The defendant is what?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: The defendant in the civil case did not appear for trial, so what happened was the judge decided to go ahead and let the plaintiffs testify, in person and over the phone, which is what Mr. Bicic did last Tuesday. So what happened is the case is not over with yet because the judge hasn't ruled. What the judge has to make the decision now is whether or not to make a ruling on the merits of the case or to enter a default judgement, which means that he enters judgement and says, "I determine that the medical evidence and all the other damages" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I just want to know the status of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: It's not over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I would like to add that it's my understanding as well that the defendant, Mr. Vukovic, has left the country, the United States, has no assets there, and also did not appoint any Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, respectfully, that's true. He did have Defence counsel. His Defence counsel withdrew Thursday before the trial started because he understood that his client had left the country and was not going to appear for trial. So that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That clears up the status of these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, I have one more question about this lawsuit and then we are going to move on to one other topic, and then you don't have to hear from me any more. Did you provide any medical information or records about this medical problem --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Oh, the microphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before the answer is given, could we have the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D6/2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, for this lawsuit in the United States that was filed and that you testified in, did you provide your lawyers with any medical -- or the Court, rather, with any medical records concerning the problem that you had, the swelling above your genital area?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember providing anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Did you provide any medical records at all?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Have any medical records been provided to the Court in this lawsuit; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, because I was asked but they had to talk directly to my family doctor in Germany, who takes care of me and my family, so that all these things are going through him. So if they addressed him, and it is not in my power to ask someone to provide anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, Mr. Bicic, I'd like to very briefly turn your attention back to your 1995 statement that you made to the OTP. Earlier you read to the Chamber the portion of your 1995 statement that dealt with the incident of Milan Simic, those four sentences you read earlier. There was no mention of Ibrahim Salkic, was there; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not mention him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: But you did testify, and it was in your statement, that Milan Simic beat you, your brother, and Perica Misic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: There was absolutely no mention anywhere in your 1995 statement that Milan Simic fired any gunshots, was there; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Then years go by, and you testify that Milan Simic -- you knew that he voluntarily surrendered himself here in late February 1998 and that immediately thereafter, someone from the OTP contacted you. And the OTP contacted you solely for the purpose of giving more details about the incident with Milan Simic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if I could have your assistance in presenting the 1998 statement in front of Mr. Bicic with, of course, the English on the ELMO and the Bosnian version in front of him. Turn to the next page -- the second page, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Bicic, could you turn to page 2, the body of the statement. Mr. Bicic, could you identify and make sure your signature is on the statement, because we haven't looked at this one yet. That's all I want to know. Is this -- do you recognise this to be your statement, Mr. Bicic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not see any signature. As for the statement, it's quite possibly mine, but there is no signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: The signature is not going to be on the Bosnian version, so why don't you look at the Bosnian version and see if you can identify that and see if that looks like your statement. Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My signature is not here either.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'm asking you to identify it. Maybe the OTP can provide a copy that they say is his statement of the 1998 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is there -- may I ask the Prosecution, is there any statement that was 1998 that was signed?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I have a two-page statement that was not signed, but I do have a two-page statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Is that his 1998 statement is all I'm asking, which they disclosed to us, just to make sure it's the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: To clarify --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to clarify, this is the same document we are speaking of, but there is no signature at all on it, and I don't believe Mr. Bicic was asked to sign it, neither on the English version or the B/C/S version. So indeed there was a document which was taken and not -- a document which was drawn up in 1998, and I think that we are speaking of the same document, but it's not a signed statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because in some cases we've had what has been described as the summary by the investigator on a statement by -- made by a witness to them, so I would like to make sure what we are dealing with is the correct type of document, whether it is a statement made by the witness or a summary by the Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honour is absolutely correct when you say that, and it may be that -- I strongly suspect that that's what happened in respect of this particular document, and that explains why it's not signed, neither in the English or the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Of course, there isn't any evidence of that, but I would imagine that that is the reason for the absence of the signatures on that 1998 document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it says "Witness Statement" clearly across the front. It has exactly the same document -- it looks exactly the same, standard OTP document as we get with every single witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: All I'm asking is that they identify it as his 1998 witness statement, just to see that we have the same document. That's all. It doesn't have to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. The fair way for the witness is to ask him to go through it at his own pace.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And at the end of it, ask him whether or not that's the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'm trying to do after asking him to look at it, does this appear to be a statement, could he identify it? That's all I'm trying to do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. Bicic, could you again look at this document, look through the information, and see if you recognise that to be your 1998 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, actually, the witness should -- you should read it, Mr. Bicic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because it's very important that we understand correctly that this is your statement or maybe it's something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Would you please read through there. Did you read the whole document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Read it silently to yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have already read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And does this appear to be the information that you discussed with the OTP in March of 1998; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. And you met with the OTP to exclusively -- to discuss exclusively the Milan Simic incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And in this 1998 statement, you added the information that wasn't in your 1995 statement that Ibrahim Salkic was also beaten by Milan Simic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And you added other details that weren't in your 1995 statement that you read here earlier today; correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: All this information that you testified to here before the Trial Chamber about bullets, that's not in your 1998 statement, is it? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may add something, I will give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Well, I want you to answer my question first and then you can add. Is there anything in there about bullets; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'll clarify it. I'll clarify it, then. You testified today about bullets - and actually, last Friday - about bullets, about Milan Simic waving his gun around, about pointing the gun at you and several other people, about hitting you with a gun in a bar, about the glass shattering, and most importantly, you testified about him shooting at least two shots. My question for you: Is any of that information in your 1998 statement; yes or no? You have the statement right in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED BICIC [Resumed]
